area_really_unique: Yes. I checked the 2508 x 2508 area picture myself: seam jump ratios 1.06/1.10 at the middle lines and 0.95/1.05 at the wrap edge. The four quadrants have a cross-correlation peak of 0.034-0.039, where a repeat would give 1.0. The whole picture's autocorrelation outside +-60 dots of zero shift peaks at 0.02. Rolled by half a picture it correlates 0.00 with itself. A bake of the same 2.5 KB description (area/descriptions/sample_101.json) in a fresh Blender process is byte-identical to the builder's colour, height and normal pictures. So the picture is 2508 dots of new content with no seam and no repeat. Its stones are the same size in dots as in the 1254 tile, so they look half as big at the 1254 preview.
variation_really_different: Different as pictures, not as looks. The 8 descriptions are exactly what sampler.py gives from S_v4 with seeds 1-8 (byte-identical when I re-ran it). They have different random seeds and counts (about 7%), radii (5%), packing and tones (+-2). A fresh bake of sample_03 is byte-identical to the builder's. Mean dot difference between variants is 33.3-35.6 (mean 34.6). A variant differs from the reference by 33-34.6, so a variant is no closer to the reference than to another variant. Best shifted correlation between any two variants is 0.044 (against the reference 0.046), so none are copies. Stone share varies 4.7% relative across variants, close to the reference's window spread of 4.5%. The recipe numbers are the same in all of them, so they are the same kind of gravel with a different arrangement, not different looks. They also all share one systematic gap from the reference: stone share about 0.61 against 0.68, and far fewer big stones (stone surviving an opening of radius 12: 0.28-0.38 against 0.516; radius 24: about 0.04 against 0.32). By eye the stones are small flat kite-shaped polygons on flat darker soil, not the chunky faceted blocks of the reference. The soil shows as a spike in the brightness curve. This agrees with the builder's own caveat, but 'as good as the fitted tile' only holds because the fitted tile has the same gap.
discrepancies: Every number I could re-run reproduces exactly. I baked 8 classes at 1254 in fresh Blender processes and scored them with lib/pixel_compare.py and lib/texture_compare.py, with a smoothed-height view written independently of the builder's score_folder.py. Bake times in the resolution table (19 / 100 / 173 s) are inflated by machine load. My own bakes took 20.8 s at 512 and 61 s at 1254. All other resolution numbers reproduce (SSIM 0.99, 1.65 and 1.68 levels, mean slope 0.374 / 0.367 / 0.352).

The dot-for-dot goal is NOT met by any procedural description. S_v4 is tier none (SSIM 0.21, Delta E 20.9, height correlation about 0) and scores worse than a flat ground colour (stage 0 of their own ladder: SSIM 0.444, Delta E 21.0). In the procedural ladder, every layer added lowers SSIM and raises Delta E. Only the same-kind score rises (0.17 to 0.44). The ladder is therefore not a rate-distortion curve for pixel accuracy. The only classes reaching tier layout are traced vector copies.

The M, T and L classes are tracing. Their descriptions are posterised, k=24 colour label maps vectorised into 2479-5431 outlines (about 121,000 outline numbers in T_k24_a50), plus about 22,900 disc stamps (x, y, r) at the reference's own speck positions in L_a100_s8. L_a100_s8 is 138,857 numbers, 9.3 % of the picture's raw byte count, and its diff sheet shows a near copy of the reference. The audit passes only because each list stays under 4000 numbers (the biggest stamp list is 3450; L_a150_s7 has 3963). The builder labels them 'traced'. Treat their scores as vector-trace quality, not procedural accuracy.
'Close' tier missed only on the normal angle (22.3 against a 12 degree limit) at L_a100_s8; the other four measures pass. The builder says this plainly.

Where Blender is used: the generator builds the flat polygon list in numpy (gravel_layers.py), meshes it with from_pydata and photographs it with an emission material. Blender is the rasteriser; the only shader-node procedural bit is the optional 'grain' noise. The tried Geometry Nodes route is a separate dead end: its texture score is 0.173 against 0.362 for the painter, and hybrids give 0.203-0.257.

The main generator never reads a picture. The only reference access is generator/geometry_route.py, via gn_tools.photograph_geometry(normal_reference='gravel'), which reads reference/gravel/normal.png to fit one normal strength number. It is a dead-end script. The scripts under analysis/ read the reference on purpose, which is allowed. Leftover files: generator/_gg_body.txt still imports slate_layers, and gravel_layers_v1_backup.py is a stale copy.

Whoever writes the guides should not describe the height blur width, normal strength or any other setting as 'used' without re-checking against S_v4.json. They should state plainly that M, T and L are tracing and that the procedural S class reaches tier none dot for dot, and they must quote the half-tile numbers as 512-dot results (my 1254 result: 0.78, 0 % over 40) and the area bake time as 205-253 s, not 173 s.
overall: The gravel numbers hold up under my own runs. All 8 claimed classes re-baked in fresh Blender processes and re-scored with lib/pixel_compare.py and lib/texture_compare.py reproduce the builder's figures exactly (SSIM, Delta E, edge skill, height error, normal angle, texture score, tier). The audit passes on every claimed description at its claimed class limit. The main generator (gravel_generator.py with gravel_layers.py and the lib helpers) reads no pictures, and a fresh S_v4, sample_03, pebbles and area bake are byte-identical to the builder's. Variations, area, resolution and transfer all check out in substance: the variants are not copies, the 2508 picture has no seam and no repeat, the same picture appears at three sizes, and the pebbles are made from numbers alone. Four caveats matter. (1) Dot-for-dot accuracy is not achieved procedurally. S_v4 is tier none and is worse than a flat colour on SSIM and Delta E. The only classes reaching tier layout (SSIM up to 0.67) are vector traces of the reference, about 359-436 KB, with the stamp lists kept just under the audit's 4000-number list limit. These are honestly labelled traced but should not be sold as procedural, and 'close' is missed only by the normal angle (22.3 against 12). (2) The two gravel guides were never written, so nothing could be checked on that side. The strips and sweep scripts have several mislabelled '(used)' values. (3) Two quoted measurements are mis-stated: the half-tile test was run at 512 dots, not 1254 (1254 gives 0.78 mean difference, 0 % over 40), and the area bake time of 173 s belongs to the resolution test (the area's own bake.json says 252.6 s). (4) The generated tiles systematically lack large stones: stone surviving an opening of radius 12 is about 0.31 against the reference's 0.52, and the stones are flat kite shapes, so 'as good as the fitted tile' means 'as far from the reference as the fitted tile'. All my files are in proc-work/recipes/gravel/verify/ (bakes, scores, and the checking scripts score_my_way.py, variation_check.py, area_check.py, half_tile_1254.py).
